text: RICOCHET combines client protection, server analytics, investigations, mitigations, and account security; the kernel driver is one component.
Activision says its internally developed kernel driver monitors and reports applications attempting to interact with protected games.
Driver installation is automatic; it starts with the game and shuts down when the game exits, according to Activision.
The kernel driver is required for PC play; the FAQ offers no driver opt-out while playing protected titles.
The stated monitoring purpose is identifying machine/process interactions that manipulate the game; this description is not a field-level telemetry specification.
The FAQ lists MW4, BO7, BO6, Warzone, MWIII, MWII, and Vanguard as protected PC titles using the driver.
Activision reports testing across varied PCs and continued iteration; no public audit or quantitative failure rate is supplied here.
RICOCHET was announced October 13, 2021, with backend protections for Vanguard and Warzone and a Warzone-first PC-driver rollout.
The driver was announced for PC; console players benefit from reduced PC cheating in cross-play, without receiving that Windows driver.
The launch promise was game-only operation and monitoring/reporting activity related to Call of Duty. This is a vendor commitment, not independent verification.
The original announcement already described ML examining server gameplay data for suspicious behavioral trends.
The December 7 announcement scheduled the driver rollout to begin in Asia-Pacific with Pacific launch, before worldwide expansion.
The December 15 progress report announced global PC-driver deployment, installed through the game update.
Damage Shield reduces a detected cheater’s ability to inflict lethal/critical damage while leaving that player vulnerable and available for investigation.
Damage Shield is described as a server-triggered response to detected tampering, not a mechanism for balancing ordinary players’ skill.
Extreme/repeated violations and attempts to disguise identity or hardware identity may result in permanent suspensions across accounts/titles.
Vanguard’s kernel driver launched globally April 26, 2022; upgrades were staged there before bringing Warzone’s driver to parity.
Cloaking hides legitimate opponents, including their relevant visual/audio cues, from detected cheaters while opponents can still see them.
Activision described both daily bans and ban waves; a single fixed ban cadence is not supported.
The report says cheating bans remove the offending player from the relevant leaderboards.
The team spans security, game/server engineering, research, and data science and collaborates with game-development teams.
Mitigations constrain detected cheaters while allowing collection and analysis; bans remain a separate enforcement outcome.
Disarm removes a detected cheater’s weapons, including fists.
Some damage still registers to preserve hit feedback and indicate the attack’s origin to the protected player.
Player reports help identify cheating trends and support investigations; the Q&A does not publish report-count thresholds.

text: The team identifies stolen/replacement accounts as part of the cheating ecosystem and recommends two-factor authentication.

text: The unified security platform introduced with MWII was intended to improve detection, mitigation development, and update frequency.
Activision described moving selected processes toward server-side execution to retain authority over more gameplay systems.
Driver updates were described as improving prevention and feeding additional information into detection and mitigation systems.
The report scheduled the driver for MWII’s October 28 and Warzone 2.0’s November 16 launch dates, globally.
The beta used only part of the security stack; full mitigations were reserved for launch. Beta behavior need not match launch behavior.
RIT reconstructs completed matches from captured/stored gameplay data for internal review; it is not described as recording the player’s desktop.
The team said it automatically captured high-tier Ranked match data and suspicious-account data across multiplayer modes.
Reports can flag accounts for review through tools including RIT.
Detection of controller-passthrough devices used to gain advantages such as recoil reduction was announced as globally deployed across platforms.
The published device-response sequence began with warnings and could escalate to mitigations, suspensions, or bans for continued misuse.
The team may adjust SR for players repeatedly benefiting from banned cheating partners, even without detecting cheats on those partners’ own machines.
Hallucinations are decoy characters supplied to flagged players and hidden from legitimate players.
They can disrupt verified cheaters or test suspicious accounts; interaction with an otherwise unseen decoy provides a detection signal.
locator: As a Mitigation; As a Detection

text: The published live design cloned an active player’s movement and presented plausible player information to cheat tools.
Quicksand slowed/froze cheaters through connection delay and could alter inputs; it was decommissioned because the visual disruption could distract legitimate players.
Configurable decoys invert the usual detection race: cheats must distinguish fake entities while defenders can vary their behavior.
The paper reports that popular cheating techniques treated the decoys as real players; this is a specific research result, not universal detection coverage.
ML assists behavioral discovery, abnormal-account challenges, action prioritization, and replay triage. The report says ML systems do not issue bans.
locator: How Does TeamRICOCHET Use Machine Learning

text: The replay model flags suspicious behavior such as wallhacks/rage cheating and prioritizes review by the team.
locator: Machine Learning x Replay Investigation Tool

text: Splat can disable a confirmed cheater’s parachute or alter velocity so a small fall becomes fatal.
Activision says player reports alone do not activate Splat and it is reserved for verified cheaters.
The report describes identifying more than 110,000 accounts exposed through reused credentials in 2023 and resetting them to prevent misuse.
